lines.home: Let's do something in the real world!
lines.away: Now go and try it. You don't need to stay here.

activities.title: Move Like an Animal
activities.short_description: Pick an animal and move like it.
activities.say: Pick an animal and move just like it!

child_steps.say: Pick an animal. An elephant? A rabbit? A tortoise?
Move slowly, like a tortoise.
Now hop quickly, like a rabbit!
Make your animal's sound, softly. Roar!

safety_notes: Clear a little floor space first.
Walk, don't run, near furniture. No jumping off things.

adaptations_by_age.3-4: Copy one animal a grown-up shows.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Invent an animal and its move.

accessibility_adaptations: Seated: move arms, head and hands only.
Picture steps need no reading.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Loud Feet, Quiet Feet
activities.short_description: Walk like a giant, then like a mouse.
activities.say: Walk like a giant, then tiptoe like a mouse!

child_steps.say: Stand in a clear spot.
Giant steps! Stomp, stomp, stomp!
Now mouse steps. Quiet, quiet feet.
When someone claps, swap!

safety_notes: Indoors on a dry floor; bare feet, not socks, on smooth tiles.
Stay away from stairs.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Lead the claps for a younger child.

accessibility_adaptations: Seated: tap hands loud and quiet on the lap.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Mirror Me
activities.short_description: Face your partner and copy every move.
activities.say: Face your partner. Copy every move, like a mirror!

child_steps.say: Stand face to face with your partner.
One person moves slowly.
The other copies, like a mirror.
Now swap who leads!

safety_notes: Slow moves only; stay an arm's length apart.

adaptations_by_age.9-10: Add a mystery move the mirror must guess.

accessibility_adaptations: Works fully seated.
The partner can be any family member, trusted adult or sibling.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: A Creature Nobody Has Seen
activities.short_description: Draw a creature nobody has ever seen.
activities.say: Draw a creature that nobody has ever seen!

child_steps.say: Get some paper and crayons.
Give your creature some funny legs.
How many eyes does it have?
Now give your creature a name!

safety_notes: Crayons rather than pens with small caps for under-4s.

adaptations_by_age.3-4: Scribble a creature and say its name.
adaptations_by_age.9-10: Draw where it lives and what it eats.

accessibility_adaptations: Can be made from paper shapes a grown-up cuts.
Telling it aloud counts too.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: A Home for a Toy
activities.short_description: Your toy needs a house. Build one!
activities.say: Your toy needs a house. Can you build one?

child_steps.say: Pick a toy that needs a home.
Find cushions or empty boxes.
Build walls and a roof.
Make a door so your toy can go in!

safety_notes: Soft things and empty cardboard only; no stacking above shoulder height.
A grown-up checks boxes for staples.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Walls, a roof and a door.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Add a garden or a second room.

accessibility_adaptations: Table-top version with blocks or folded paper.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Cloud Shapes
activities.short_description: Look at the sky. What shapes can you see?
activities.say: Look at the sky. What shapes can you see in the clouds?

child_steps.say: Go to a window.
Find one big cloud.
What does it look like? A sheep? A dragon?
Watch it slowly change shape.

safety_notes: Never look at the sun.
Stay inside at the window, or go out with a grown-up.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Notice which way the clouds move.

accessibility_adaptations: If the sky is clear, notice birds, trees or the sky's colour instead.
Seated by the window works.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Which Rolls Farther?
activities.short_description: Guess which one rolls the farthest!
activities.say: Guess which one will roll the farthest. Then try it!

child_steps.say: Get a ball, an orange and a steel tumbler.
Which one will roll the farthest? Guess!
Roll each one gently on the floor.
Which one went the farthest? Were you surprised?

safety_notes: Flat floor away from stairs and glass; steel tumbler, not glass.
No marbles or small balls.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Try a slope made from a book.

accessibility_adaptations: A grown-up can roll while the child guesses and watches.
Seated works.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Sock Partners
activities.short_description: These socks lost their partners. Help them!
activities.say: These socks lost their partners. Can you help them?

child_steps.say: Get a pile of clean socks.
Find two that are the same.
Put the partners together.
Put them in the basket. All done!

safety_notes: Clean, dry laundry only; keep away from detergent.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Sort them by who they belong to.

accessibility_adaptations: Works seated.
Match by touch for a child with low vision.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Story Chain
activities.short_description: Make a story together, one bit each.
activities.say: Make a story together. You say one bit, they say the next!

child_steps.say: Sit with a family member or a grown-up you trust.
You start: Once upon a time...
Now they add the next bit.
Take turns until the story ends!

safety_notes: No personal questions or secrets.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Add a problem the hero must solve.
adaptations_by_age.9-10: The story must use three chosen objects.

accessibility_adaptations: A picture card like monkey, tree and bus can start it.
Signs and gestures count as turns.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Five Things I Can See
activities.short_description: Look around slowly. Find five things.
activities.say: Look around slowly. Can you find five things?

child_steps.say: Sit or stand comfortably.
Find something blue.
Find something round.
Now count five things you can see!

safety_notes: No eyes-closed or breathing instructions; stop any time.

adaptations_by_age.3-4: Find two things with a grown-up.

accessibility_adaptations: A child with low vision can find five things to touch or hear.
activities.approved_by: parent, 17 Nov 2026

activities.title: Three Baskets at Home
activities.short_description: Sort things into three baskets.
activities.say: Sort things into three baskets. Let's see how!

child_steps.say: Put out three baskets.
Pick a pile of toys or steel things.
Make three groups. Which things go together?
Tell a grown-up why they go together.

safety_notes: Big toys and steel kitchen things only; no small parts, glass or sharp things.
A grown-up checks the pile first.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Three baskets; the child picks the rule.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Sort again by a new rule.

accessibility_adaptations: Seated on the floor works.
Sort by touch if sight is low.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Make Ten with Spoons
activities.short_description: Two piles of spoons that make ten.
activities.say: Make two piles of spoons that make ten!

child_steps.say: Count ten spoons. One, two, three...
Put some on each plate.
Count each plate. How many?
Now make ten a new way!

safety_notes: Steel spoons only, no knives or forks.
A grown-up fetches the spoons.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Find two or three ways to make ten.
adaptations_by_age.6-7: Find every way; say 7 and 3 make ten.

accessibility_adaptations: A grown-up can point while the child counts aloud.
Seated at a table works.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Window Tally
activities.short_description: Count birds or vehicles with tally marks.
activities.say: Count what passes the window. Make a mark for each one!

child_steps.say: Sit at a window.
Pick cars or birds to count.
Make one mark for each one.
Count your marks. Which had most?

safety_notes: Stay inside at the window; keep it closed or with a grille.
Crayon, not a pen.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Count one thing for a few minutes.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Count two things and compare; bundle marks in fives.

accessibility_adaptations: A grown-up can mark while the child tells.
Listen for vehicles if sight is low.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Draw a Maze for Appa or Amma
activities.short_description: Draw a path for a grown-up to follow.
activities.say: Draw a winding path. Can Appa or Amma follow it?

child_steps.say: Get paper and a crayon.
Mark a start and a finish.
Draw a winding path between them.
Ask Appa or Amma to follow it!

safety_notes: Crayons only; a grown-up sits close by.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Add dead ends, then say left and right turns.

accessibility_adaptations: Trace the path with a finger.
A grown-up can draw while the child gives directions.

en.title: Draw a Maze for Appa or Amma

activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Seed in a Cup
activities.short_description: Plant a seed and watch it for a week.
activities.say: Plant a seed in a cup and watch it grow!

child_steps.say: Put soil in the cup.
Press a seed into the soil.
Give it a little water.
Put it by a bright window.
Look every day. What changed?

safety_notes: Wash hands with soap after touching soil or seeds.
Seeds are not for eating; keep them away from younger siblings.
A grown-up checks the soil is clean.

adaptations_by_age.3-4: Plant with help and look each day.
adaptations_by_age.5-6: Water it and tell what it needs.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Draw it each day for a week.

accessibility_adaptations: Seated at a table works.
Feel the soil if sight is low.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Shadow Tracing
activities.short_description: Trace a toy's shadow, then again later.
activities.say: Trace your toy's shadow. Then look again later!

child_steps.text: Put a toy in the sun
child_steps.say: Put a toy in the sunlight.
Trace the shadow with a crayon.
Wait until later in the day.
Trace it again. What changed?

safety_notes: Stay inside by a sunny window or go out with a grown-up.
Never look at the sun.
Crayon only.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Trace twice and say what changed.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Trace three times and guess where it moves next.

accessibility_adaptations: A grown-up can hold the paper still.
Seated by the window works.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Rupee Shop
activities.short_description: Play shop with toy prices of one to five rupees.
activities.say: Let's play shop! Toys cost one to five rupees.

materials.name: paper coins or a few real coins

child_steps.say: Put a price on each toy.
Get your paper coins.
Choose a toy and pay.
Now swap! Who is the shopkeeper?

safety_notes: Paper coins are best. Real coins only with a grown-up watching.
Coins are a choking risk for little ones; count them before and after, and put them away.
Keep coins out of the mouth.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Prices one to three; pay with paper coins.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Prices up to five; work out change.

accessibility_adaptations: A grown-up can count coins aloud with the child.
Sort coins by touch.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Sound Hunt
activities.short_description: Find three things that start with the same sound.
activities.say: Find three things that start with the same sound!

child_steps.say: Banana starts with buh. Say buh!
Look around for something with buh.
Show it to a grown-up. Say its name.
Find three things with buh!

safety_notes: Carry only safe things; leave glass, knives and hot things.
A grown-up helps with high shelves.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Hunt a new sound each round.

accessibility_adaptations: Say the names aloud together.
Point instead of fetching if moving is hard.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Left Hand, Right Foot
activities.short_description: Simon says with left and right.
activities.say: Simon says! Move your left or right hand and foot!

child_steps.say: Stand in a clear spot.
Simon says, raise your right hand!
Simon says, tap your left foot.
Now you be Simon!

safety_notes: Clear floor, no furniture nearby.
Slow moves; no hopping or spinning.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: One hand or foot at a time.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Cross over and do two moves at once.

accessibility_adaptations: Seated: use hands only.
A coloured band marks the right hand.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Number Hop
activities.short_description: Hop to the number that is called out.
activities.say: Hop to the number you hear! One, two, three!

child_steps.say: Put numbers one to ten down.
Listen for a number.
Hop to that number!
Now you call a number.

safety_notes: Dry floor; tape paper down so it does not slide.
Small hops only, no jumping from furniture.
Chalk only outdoors on a clear path.

adaptations_by_age.7-8: Numbers one to ten; hop the sum of two numbers.

accessibility_adaptations: Seated: point or tap the number.
Large numbers help low vision.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Question Ball
activities.short_description: Pass a soft ball and answer a question.
activities.say: Pass the soft ball. Whoever holds it answers!

materials.name: a soft ball or rolled socks

child_steps.say: Sit in a circle.
Roll the soft ball to someone.
Ask: What is your favourite food?
Answer, then roll it on!

safety_notes: Soft ball or rolled socks only; roll along the floor.
Keep questions simple and happy; no private questions.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Questions about food, colours and animals.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Ask why, and tell a little story.

accessibility_adaptations: Answer by pointing or showing.
Any language at home is welcome.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)

activities.title: Shape Picture
activities.short_description: Make a picture from paper shapes.
activities.say: Make a picture out of paper shapes!

materials.name: paper shapes cut by a grown-up

child_steps.say: Ask a grown-up to cut shapes.
Pick circles, squares and triangles.
Make a house, a bus or a cat.
Stick it down with a glue stick.

safety_notes: A grown-up does all the cutting; the child never uses scissors.
Glue stick only; tidy up the paper scraps.
Keep small scraps from younger siblings.

adaptations_by_age.5-6: Build a picture and name each shape.
adaptations_by_age.7-8: Make a scene with ten shapes.

accessibility_adaptations: Big shapes are easier to hold.
Telling the picture aloud counts.
activities.approved_by: Claude review 24 Nov 2026 (owner asked Claude to review)
